written:
## 1. The numbers
Cautious, with risk-off leanings. Traders are positioning for a December Fed rate hike. Tech held up better than the Dow, which was dragged down by health care.

## 2. What moved and why
**S&P 500 slips as tech's early gains fade ahead of Anthropic's debut**
Why it happened: Tech stocks gave up most of their early gains by late morning. Health insurers also sold off on a proposed Medicare Advantage audit plan.
Why it matters: A hot AI listing did not lift the wider market, which suggests buyers are more selective.

**Fed hike bets firm up while US factory data weakens**
Why it happened: Fed minutes and speeches by Fed officials pointed to higher rates ahead. Governor Waller said the Fed should either approve a half-point hike in December or signal faster hikes in 2027.
Why it matters: Higher policy rates hit gold and stretched equity valuations, and they put pressure on the Bank of Canada too.

**Gold slides below $3,700 on yields and a firm dollar**
Why it happened: Higher Treasury yields and a stronger dollar have raised the opportunity cost of holding gold.
Why it matters: Gold is not acting as a safe haven, and the selloff is hurting Canadian miners.

## Deals
- **IPO: Anthropic → Public markets (ticker ANT)** (About $81.34 billion). Priced at $83 a share, above its planned range, raising about $81.34 billion. It is a very large AI listing, and demand was strong enough to price above the range.
- **Acquisition: Mitsui Chemicals → JSR** (About ¥1.84T (~$11.6B)). The deal is described as strategically compelling but heavily leveraged.
- **Acquisition: Shield AI → Echodyne** (Up to $5.3B). A defence-technology deal in which Shield AI would buy a radar maker.

## Already out today
- 8:30 AM: US weekly jobless claims. 203,000 vs 197,000 expected. Layoffs remain low.
- 8:30 AM: Philadelphia Fed manufacturing index. 6.3 vs about 20.6 expected. Factory growth cooled sharply.
- 10:00 AM: Conference Board Leading Economic Index (October). Down 0.3% vs no change expected. This points to a softer outlook.

## 3. What's coming today
- Today: Earnings from Walmart, Alibaba, PDD, Intuit and NetEase. These are listed on today's results calendar. They give a read on consumers and China.
- Later today (time TBC): Anthropic's first trade. This is the test for AI IPO demand.
- 12:30 PM: Chicago Fed's Goolsbee speaks. Clues on the December hike. Also today: Barkin at 2 PM, Barr at 2:15 PM, Paulson at 6:30 PM.
- Wed 8:30 AM: US core PCE. Prior reading 3.1%. It is the Fed's preferred inflation gauge.

## 4. Canada corner
- The TSX fell 2.1% on Wednesday to 34,578.05, its lowest close since June 10. Materials, energy and financials led the losses.
- The loonie trades near 70 US cents. A firm US dollar and lower commodity prices are pressuring it.
- Bank of Canada: October CPI was 3.1%, unchanged from September. The probability of a December hike has returned to around 50%, according to Commerzbank.

## 5. The takeaway
If someone asks you about markets today: stocks are softer because markets are pricing a December Fed hike. That is pressuring gold and the TSX's resource-heavy index, while the AI trade is holding up better than the broader market.
Consulting angle: The Medicare Advantage audit proposal is a regulatory risk for insurers. A strong answer covers coding accuracy, repayment scenarios and how to adjust pricing and benefits.
Accounting angle: If clawbacks apply to past years, insurers would need to estimate refund liabilities against previously booked revenue. Auditors would test the estimates and disclosures.

2. [US Stock Market Today (Yahoo Finance)](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/stocks/articles/us-stock-market-today-p-131516375.html)
3. [Stock Market News for Nov 19 (Yahoo Finance)](https://au.finance.yahoo.com/news/stock-market-news-nov-19-132100065.html)
4. [Dow, S&P 500 ahead of Anthropic debut (Yahoo Finance)](https://finance.yahoo.com/markets/live/stock-market-today-thursday-november-19-dow-sp-500-nasdaq-anthropic-ipo-live-141306032.html)
5. [Gold's bad year is getting worse (CNBC)](https://www.cnbc.com/2026/11/19/gold-prices-fall-fed-rates-dollar.html)

stories.title: S&P 500 slips as tech's early gains fade ahead of Anthropic's debut
stories.why_happened: Tech stocks gave up most of their early gains by late morning. Health insurers also sold off on a proposed Medicare Advantage audit plan.
stories.why_matters: A hot AI listing did not lift the wider market, which suggests buyers are more selective.
stories.full: The S&P 500 had fallen five days in a row through Wednesday as investors digested NVIDIA's earnings and waited for Anthropic's IPO. Futures pointed higher this morning, and the Nasdaq 100 fund was up 2.06% at 10:04 a.m. ET. By 11:05 a.m. ET, it was up only 0.41%. The Dow did worse than the S&P. Humana and UnitedHealth fell on a proposed CMS audit programme aimed at Medicare Advantage overpayments, with worries about retroactive clawbacks. UnitedHealth is a Dow member, so its drop pulled the index down. Anthropic is the winner on the day in terms of capital raised. CNBC said the IPO had failed to revive enthusiasm for AI stocks. Health insurers with large Medicare Advantage books are the losers until the rules are clearer. Watch Anthropic's first-day trading and the final form of the CMS proposal.

stories.title: Fed hike bets firm up while US factory data weakens
stories.why_happened: Fed minutes and speeches by Fed officials pointed to higher rates ahead. Governor Waller said the Fed should either approve a half-point hike in December or signal faster hikes in 2027.
stories.why_matters: Higher policy rates hit gold and stretched equity valuations, and they put pressure on the Bank of Canada too.
stories.full: The Fed held its rate at 3.75%-4.00% last month. Markets now expect a hike. CME FedWatch showed about a 90% chance of a quarter-point rise and 10% for a half-point at the December 8–9 meeting. St. Louis Fed's Musalem said several increases may be needed before spring 2027. Today's data mixed growth and price signals. The Philadelphia Fed index fell to 6.3, its lowest since May, from 20.9. Prices received reached their highest level since June 2022. Weaker growth with rising prices makes the Fed's job harder. The 10-year yield eased slightly but stays high. Winners are savers and the dollar. Losers are rate-sensitive sectors and non-yielding assets. Watch core PCE next Wednesday and any further Fed speeches.

stories.why_happened: Higher Treasury yields and a stronger dollar have raised the opportunity cost of holding gold.
stories.why_matters: Gold is not acting as a safe haven, and the selloff is hurting Canadian miners.
stories.full: Gold hit a record $5,589.38 in January. On Wednesday it fell below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025, and today it dropped below $3,700. The old logic of gold as a hedge against inflation and geopolitics has weakened. The conflict pushed oil and inflation higher, which fuelled bets on higher interest rates. Those rate bets lift the dollar and make non-yielding gold less attractive. Miners and gold ETF holders lose the most. TSX materials stocks fell 5.4% on Wednesday. Analysts disagree on what comes next. One expects $3,500 to $3,600. The World Gold Council points to $3,605 as potential support. Watch the dollar, Treasury yields and core PCE.

intern.headline: Fed rate hike bets weigh on stocks and gold
intern.mood: Cautious. Investors are getting ready for a possible interest rate hike (a rise in the rate set by the central bank) in December. Tech held up better than the Dow, which was pulled down by health care stocks.

stories.title: S&P 500 slips as tech's early gains fade ahead of Anthropic's debut
stories.why_happened: Tech stocks gave up most of their early gains by late morning. Health insurers also sold off on a proposed Medicare Advantage audit plan (a government plan to check payments to private health insurers).
stories.why_matters: A hot AI listing did not lift the wider market. This suggests buyers are being more careful and picky.
stories.full: The S&P 500 (a index of 500 large US companies, used to track the market) had fallen five days in a row through Wednesday. Investors were digesting NVIDIA's earnings (the company's profit report) and waiting for Anthropic's IPO (the first time a company sells its shares to the public). Futures (contracts that show where the market may open) pointed higher this morning. The Nasdaq 100 fund was up 2.06% at 10:04 a.m. ET. By 11:05 a.m. ET, it was up only 0.41%. The Dow did worse than the S&P. Humana and UnitedHealth fell on a proposed CMS audit programme. CMS is the US agency that runs Medicare. The audit targets Medicare Advantage overpayments (extra payments insurers may have received). Investors also worried about retroactive clawbacks (having to pay back money for past years). UnitedHealth is a Dow member, so its drop pulled the index down. Anthropic is the winner of the day in terms of money raised. CNBC said the IPO had failed to revive excitement for AI stocks. Health insurers with large Medicare Advantage businesses are the losers until the rules are clearer. Watch Anthropic's first-day trading and the final form of the CMS proposal.

stories.title: Fed rate hike bets firm up while US factory data weakens
stories.why_happened: Fed minutes (notes from the central bank's meetings) and speeches by Fed officials pointed to higher rates ahead. Governor Waller said the Fed should either approve a half-point hike in December or signal faster hikes in 2027.
stories.why_matters: Higher interest rates hit gold and make stock prices look expensive. They also put pressure on the Bank of Canada too.
stories.full: The Fed (the US central bank) held its rate at 3.75%-4.00% last month. Markets now expect a hike. CME FedWatch (a tool that shows what traders expect the Fed to do) showed about a 90% chance of a quarter-point rise and 10% for a half-point rise at the December 8-9 meeting. St. Louis Fed's Musalem said several increases may be needed before spring 2027. Today's data mixed growth and price signals. The Philadelphia Fed index fell to 6.3, its lowest since May, from 20.9. This index measures how factories in the region are doing. Prices received (what factories are charging for their goods) reached their highest level since June 2022. Weaker growth with rising prices makes the Fed's job harder. The 10-year yield (the interest rate on 10-year government bonds) eased slightly but stays high. Winners are savers and the dollar. Losers are rate-sensitive sectors (industries that do badly when rates rise) and non-yielding assets (things that pay no interest or income, such as gold). Watch core PCE (the Fed's preferred inflation gauge) next Wednesday and any further Fed speeches.

stories.title: Gold slides below $3,700 on yields and a firm dollar
stories.why_happened: Higher Treasury yields (the interest rates on US government debt) and a stronger dollar have raised the opportunity cost (what you give up by choosing one option over another) of holding gold.
stories.why_matters: Gold is not acting as a safe haven (an asset people buy to protect their money in hard times). The selloff is hurting Canadian miners.
stories.full: Gold hit a record $5,589.38 in January. On Wednesday it fell below $3,800 for the first time since September 2025. Today it dropped below $3,700. The old idea of gold as a hedge against inflation (protection when prices rise) and geopolitics (protection against world conflict) has weakened. The conflict pushed oil and inflation higher. This fuelled bets on higher interest rates. Those rate bets lift the dollar and make non-yielding gold less attractive. Miners and gold ETF holders (people who own funds that track gold prices) lose the most. TSX materials stocks fell 5.4% on Wednesday. Analysts disagree on what comes next. One expects $3,500 to $3,600. The World Gold Council points to $3,605 as a possible support level (a price where buyers may step in). Watch the dollar, Treasury yields and core PCE.

Trading is expected today after the market opens at 9:30 a.m. ET. The shares were priced at $83 each, above the planned range. The IPO shows money is still available for AI companies. But what happens after the IPO matters too. Cerebras fell after renewed attention on IPOs trading below their offer prices (the price set before shares start trading). I found no reported valuation figure (the total value of the company).

The high multiple shows buyers will pay up for AI-linked supply chains. Defence tech buyers are adding sensors to their autonomy software (the programs that let machines act on their own). I found no valuation multiple.

Trading is expected today after the market opens at 9:30 a.m. ET. The IPO shows capital is still available for AI, but the aftermarket matters. Cerebras fell after renewed attention on IPOs trading below their offer prices. I found no reported valuation figure.

deals.why: The deal is described as strategically compelling but heavily leveraged. Second-order: roughly 16x expected EBITDA with net debt temporarily above 4x sets up a refinancing of the bridge into term debt, a live test of Japanese leveraged-M&A financing appetite and of how the market prices AI-linked materials assets.
deals.full: Mitsui is paying roughly 16 times expected EBITDA, financed by a ¥1.64T bridge loan that temporarily pushes net debt above four times EBITDA. That implies Mitsui will need to refinance the bridge loan with longer-term debt. The logic is to move into semiconductor materials, a segment tied to chip demand. The high multiple shows buyers will pay up for AI-linked supply chains. Closing is expected in the second half of the fiscal year ending March 2028, subject to regulatory approvals.

deals.why: A defence-technology deal in which Shield AI would buy a radar maker. Second-order: sensor-plus-autonomy consolidation is pulling defence-tech valuations up, and the 'up to' headline implies an earn-out structure that shifts risk and dilutes the headline multiple.
deals.full: Shield AI would pay up to $5.3 billion for Echodyne. "Up to" often means part of the price depends on future milestones, but my sources did not give the structure. Defence tech buyers are adding sensors to their autonomy software. I found no valuation multiple.
